name: Colonnade-Tempest
geological_features: Columnar convection cells creating parallel storm walls
specific_features: Parallel storm walls visible from orbit resembling a colonnade
description: Colonnade-Tempest is a massive gas giant whose atmospheric dynamics produce a feature unique in the cataloged systems: parallel walls of storm activity that line up along the planet's longitudinal lines, creating a columnar pattern visible from orbit that resembles a colonnade wrapped around the equator. These storm walls are thousands of kilometers tall and extend for tens of thousands of kilometers in length, separated by calmer channels of relatively clear atmosphere.

The toxic atmosphere roars with the energy of a world that generates more heat than it receives. The storm walls are barriers of lightning, wind, and compressed gas that probe encounters have measured at sustained velocities exceeding three thousand kilometers per hour. The channels between them are deceptively calm, their apparent stillness masking turbulence that would shred any conventional vessel. The planet's color palette is dominated by dark reds and burnt oranges, giving it a menacing appearance even from a safe distance.

The colonnade pattern results from the interaction between the planet's rapid rotation and an unusual internal heat distribution that creates longitudinal convection cells rather than the typical latitudinal banding. This pattern is not predicted by standard atmospheric models and has prompted revisions to gas giant formation theory. The planet's extensive moon system includes three large bodies with their own geological interest, one of which shows evidence of a subsurface ocean.

Colonnade-Tempest's extreme conditions make it the most challenging helium-3 harvesting target in the sector, but its reserves are proportionally the largest. No current technology can operate safely within the storm walls, and even the calm channels present risks beyond acceptable thresholds. The planet remains a target for the next generation of harvesting technology, its resources effectively locked behind an atmospheric fortress.
